Appendix 1: eligible Irish higher education institutions

summary: The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship is funded by the Irish Government with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority. About 60 one-year scholarships are expected for 2026/27 for high-calibre students from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK who already hold an offer for a full-time, in-person master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD (NFQ levels 9 or 10) in Ireland. It gives a stipend of EUR 10,000 and a full fee waiver from the host institution for the scholarship year.
eligibility_notes:
An applicant must meet all four conditions. First, domiciliary of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. Domiciliary of origin means the country of legal and permanent residence before the call deadline; it is not the same as nationality and it does not change during studies. UK citizens and Russian and Belarusian citizens are not eligible; studying in Russia or Belarus does not by itself make someone ineligible.

Second, an offer of a place as an international, fee-paying student on a full-time, in-person course at an eligible Irish institution: a taught master's of at least one year, a postgraduate diploma at NFQ level 9 of at least one year, or a research master's or PhD of at least one year. Online degrees, undergraduate degrees, foundation year studies and courses starting in winter or spring are not eligible. Blended courses count only if the scholar attends all in-person classes and lives in Ireland throughout. Northern Ireland institutions are not eligible.

Third, the applicant has never held a GOI-IES scholarship (people who applied unsuccessfully before may apply again). Fourth, not a Russian or Belarusian citizen.

The offer must be in hand when the application is submitted, with proof attached. Conditional and final offers are both accepted, but some institutions prefer final offers when shortlisting. The offer must be for the 2026/27 academic year (deferred students and current PhD or two-year master's students attach a document from their institution confirming study in 2026/27). Only one offer document and one eligible application per candidate; more than one leads to disqualification of all applications.

There is no age limit and no English language certificate is needed for the GOI-IES application itself (the institution may ask for one for admission). Refugees and asylum seekers may apply under the same rules. Final-year undergraduates may apply if they hold a postgraduate offer. Applicants should check with the institution that their course accepts GOI-IES scholars.
age_experience_notes: No age limit. Work experience is scored as part of the 'academic qualifications, achievements and work experience' section.
funding_summary: A stipend of EUR 10,000 for one year of study as a contribution to student costs and living expenses, paid through the host institution, plus a full fee waiver (tuition fee and registration charge) from the host institution for the scholarship year. The scholarship is not extended beyond one academic year, although an institution may choose to extend the fee waiver for a course that runs three semesters. There is no travel or study-materials funding and no support for dependants.
programmes_note: All disciplines, subject to places. Master's (taught or research), postgraduate diploma at NFQ level 9 and PhD, full-time and in person, lasting at least one year. The institutions decide which of their courses accept GOI-IES scholars and give fee waivers, so the course must be checked with the institution. No programme list is published by the funder.
institutions_note: Eligible institutions in 2026 (Appendix 1): Atlantic Technological University, CCT College, Dublin Business School, Dublin City University, Dun Laoghaire Institute of Art, Design and Technology, Dundalk Institute of Technology, Griffith College, ICD Business School, Independent College, Mary Immaculate College, Maynooth University, Munster Technological University, National College of Art and Design, National College of Ireland, RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences, South East Technological University, Technological University Dublin, Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands Midwest, Trinity College Dublin, University College Cork, University College Dublin, University of Galway and University of Limerick. The applicant applies for admission to the institution separately. There is an upper limit of five awards per institution.

summary.detail: Taught master's of at least one year, or research master's of at least one year, full-time and in person at NFQ level 9.
summary.source_text: taught master's degree programme which is at least one year long

summary.detail: PhD or research programme of at least one year, full-time and in person (NFQ level 10). The scholarship covers one year only. PhD applicants must find a supervisor themselves; the funder does not help.
summary.source_text: a research programme (i.e. research master's or PhD)

summary.detail: Postgraduate diploma at NFQ level 9 of at least one year, full-time and in person.
summary.source_text: a postgraduate diploma at NFQ level 9

benefits.limit_text: EUR 10,000 for one year of study
benefits.conditions: A contribution towards student costs and living expenses; the call document says it is unlikely to cover living costs fully. Sent to the host institution in two instalments of EUR 5,000 (semester 1 and semester 2); the institution passes it on in the same instalments or in smaller monthly payments. The first stipend is expected towards the end of October 2026, so own funds are needed for the first weeks.

benefits.limit_text: Full fee waiver for the scholarship year: tuition fee and registration charge
benefits.conditions: Given by the host institution as its matched funding. The institution may extend the waiver for courses of three semesters. Application fees are not waived. A deposit that forms part of tuition fees must be refunded.

benefits.limit_text: No funding for travel to Ireland
benefits.conditions: The FAQs state there is no funding for travelling to Ireland or for study materials.

benefits.limit_text: No funding for study materials and no support for relatives or dependants
benefits.conditions: Visas for family members may not be approved.

requirements.text: Proof of admission: an offer letter, an offer email from the institution's Admissions Office, or a screenshot of the applicant portal confirming the offer, for an eligible course in the 2026/27 academic year. Conditional or final offers are accepted. Only one offer per application.
Document from the institution confirming a deferral to 2026/27, or confirming continued study in 2026/27 for current PhD and two-year master's students.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for deferred students and students already enrolled at an eligible institution.

requirements.text: Completed online application form in English: preliminary eligibility questions, academic history and work experience, details of the offer (including the student or application number from the institution), and the personal statement. Some sections have word limits shown in the portal.

Two references, uploaded by the applicant through the portal (referees cannot upload them; references sent any other way are not accepted). Each of 500 to 700 words, in English (notarised translation accepted), dated no more than a year before the call closing date, with an official header, the referee's organisational postal address and email, and a handwritten or electronic signature (typed names are not accepted). Referees must not be family or have a financial or close personal tie to the applicant.

application_steps.title: Apply for admission to an eligible Irish institution first
application_steps.detail: Choose a full-time, in-person master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD of at least one year at an eligible institution, check that it accepts GOI-IES scholars, and apply through the institution's own admission process (the scholarship form does not give admission). You need an offer in hand before applying for the scholarship; PhD applicants find their own supervisor.

application_steps.title: Create an account and pass the eligibility check
application_steps.detail: Use the GOI-IES online portal. The form starts with three eligibility questions (domiciliary of origin, offer from an eligible institution as a full-time non-EU paying student, previous GOI-IES). Ineligible answers stop the application. Only one eligible application is allowed; setting up several accounts is treated as fraud.

application_steps.title: Complete the form, upload offer and references, and submit
application_steps.detail: Fill in academic history, work experience and the personal statement, attach the offer document and two references, and submit by 5pm Irish time on 12 March 2026 (2026 call). Nothing can be changed after submission and late applications are not accepted. The application must be the applicant's own work; drafting by others and AI-generated content are prohibited. Questions go to the HEA mailbox by 5 March 2026.

application_steps.title: HEA and institution checks and shortlisting
application_steps.detail: The HEA screens eligibility, then shares applications with the institutions named. They run further checks and shortlist according to their international strategy (for example country of origin, study level, capacity and field of study).

application_steps.title: Independent panel scores shortlisted applications
application_steps.detail: An independent panel scores only the submitted material: academic qualifications, achievements and work experience (40 marks), personal statement (45 marks: 15 each for benefit of the scholarship, involvement in Irish society and promoting the scheme, and long-term interest in Ireland) and two references (15 marks). A minimum of 60 marks is needed. The top 12 ranked applications are funded on excellence, with up to five awards per institution. Results are expected in early June 2026, and there is no individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Confirm the award, prepare for Ireland and apply for a visa
application_steps.detail: Successful candidates get an official award letter from the HEA. The institution must confirm it can give the fee waiver. The award is rescinded if a conditional offer is not met, and it cannot be moved to another course or institution except in a case approved by the HEA where the course is cancelled. Visa applications should start as soon as the award letter arrives, because late arrival can cost the scholarship.

application_steps.title: Start in September or October and live in Ireland
application_steps.detail: Scholars start in September or October 2026 and must live in Ireland for the whole of their studies. The stipend is paid in two EUR 5,000 instalments through the institution. An awarding event is planned for spring 2027. There are no formal obligations after finishing, such as returning to the home country.
